stories.headline: Ballard of a Busy Autumn for test31
stories.deck: test31's Ballard talks up Northern Ireland's four-game Nations League run
stories.body:
test31's Ballard is talking up Northern Ireland's Nations League block, four matches at short notice, and by his own account a squad with "a lot of talent and hunger". That is a defender happy to be involved, which is more minutes and more exposure over a compressed international window.

What it does to test31 is unstated. The wire gives no fitness line and no risk, only that the schedule is heavy. For now he is a defender in demand for his country and nothing more can be read into it.

stories.headline: Egan the Hull of the Matter for test1
stories.deck: test1's John Egan the subject of a BBC feature on his return to the Premier League with Hull City
stories.body:
The wire has John Egan back in the top flight with Hull City, and back in Heimir Hallgrimsson's Ireland set-up with it. For everyone else it reads as a nice career note. For test1 it is a name on the sheet climbing back into games that count.

What it does for the return is another matter, and the copy does not say. A defender in a promoted side is a defender in a promoted side. test1 have the ownership; they wait on the minutes.

stories.headline: testf Left Waiting on a Certificate Check
stories.deck: Xhaka, owned by testf, under investigation over his Covid-19 vaccination certificate; no line on availability.
stories.body:
The wire has Granit Xhaka under investigation over an issue with his Covid-19 vaccination certificate. He is testf's, and that is the whole of the draft stake: the league leaders in points scored have a captain in the headlines for something no one has yet attached a timescale to.

What it costs testf, nobody can say. The report offers no ban, no missed fixture, no line on availability. Until it does, Xhaka is a name in an investigation and not a name out of a line-up, and testf plan around him as before.

stories.headline: Friday Pressers
stories.deck: Luka Vušković fit again for Brighton, with Hadjam back and Dunk a rotation doubt
stories.body:
Fabian Hurzeler declared Luka Vušković fit again and back in contention, Brighton's clearest gain before the deadline. He stopped short of naming a line-up, and left Lewis Dunk's involvement open with rotation on the table.

Jaouen Hadjam returns alongside Vušković, so Hurzeler has options restored at the back that he did not have a week ago.

teamNews.line: Unai Emery ruled out Marco Bizot and left a question mark over Joao Gomes.
Harry Wilson goes into the weekend under a cloud.
Nothing new from Crystal Palace ahead of the deadline.
Kenny Tete will not feature for Fulham.
Manchester United added nothing to a settled list.
David Moyes ruled Merlin Röhl out without detailing the reason.
Roberto De Zerbi left Pedro Porro's involvement in doubt.
Mikel Arteta welcomed two men back into contention.
Fabian Hurzeler had two fit again and stopped short of committing to Lewis Dunk.

stories.headline: Thursday Pressers
stories.deck: João Pedro a Chelsea doubt for the deadline, no complaint given
stories.body:
João Pedro sits as a doubt for Chelsea, with Xabi Alonso stopping short of clearing him and giving no update on what keeps him on the edge of it.

Whether test211's man features is a decision left open, and nothing said points to a timescale.

teamNews.line: Xabi Alonso would not commit either way on João Pedro before the deadline.
Matthias Jaissle flagged Amar Dedic as a fitness question.
Sergej Jakirovic left Matt Targett uncertain for the weekend.
Frank Lampard ruled Aurèle Amenda out entirely.
Nothing new came out of Nottingham Forest.
Brentford added nothing to their list.

stories.headline: Lawro's Predictions: GW6
stories.deck: Lawro goes against the favourites in test3 v test2, and leaves test4 v 123 to the front-runners.
stories.body: First column here, and no record to answer for yet. That comes soon enough. Twenty-two years of Saturday scores on the BBC, and now this. Preston weather, then.

ties.line: test3 are the favourites, and I fancy test2 anyway. Why? Isak. He is up against Manchester City, a tough defence, and none of that bothers a Liverpool man one bit. Gonzalo of Fulham has gone quiet for test3, no goal and no assist in his last two. Havertz of Arsenal has done the same for test2, so that pair cancel out. Both lost last week. Sitting through this one will feel like waiting for a bus that never turns up. I'll go with test2.

123 top the table and look the part. Haaland of Manchester City has scored in each of his last two. Good news? Not for test4. Mbeumo of Manchester United has gone dry for test4, no goal and no assist in two. Fernandes of Manchester United, same story for 123, so it's not all one way. Foden is suspended for test4, and that's that. Both sides came off a win last week. I'd be surprised if the front-runners slipped here. 123 for me.

stories.headline: Maguire In The Dock For test3
stories.deck: test3's Maguire caught up in the Man City verdict fallout; no draft consequence stated.
stories.body:
The wire has Kieran Maguire, owned by test3, fielding listener questions on the Man City verdict alongside Dale Johnson. That is the sum of it: a name test3 holds, attached to the story the whole league already knows.

Nothing in the copy touches minutes, fitness or return. test3 reads it as we do and takes nothing from it beyond the reminder that the asset is his.

stories.headline: Hall And Dewsbury-Hall Hit The Books
stories.deck: Hall (test2) and Dewsbury-Hall (Notemail) are studying to be sporting directors alongside playing.
stories.body:
test2 and Notemail own two men filing coursework from the team bus. Hall, on test2's books, and Dewsbury-Hall, on Notemail's, feature among the Premier League players reading for the sporting director trade while they play.

Nothing in the wire touches availability, and neither should this. No absence, no timeline, no minutes lost. Both remain what they were to their managers, only now they carry a textbook on the away trips.

stories.headline: Brobbey's treble no robbery
stories.deck: Manchester City beat Sunderland 5-3

reports.standfirst: Manchester City beat Sunderland 5-3 to stay top with a fifth win running, Brian Brobbey's hat-trick counting for nothing.
reports.account:
Brian Brobbey scored three times for Sunderland and finished on the losing side.
Nilson Angulo shot wide from inside the box after Enzo Le Fée crossed, in the 6th minute.
Enzo Fernández put Manchester City ahead after nine minutes, and Brobbey answered three minutes later, taking a through ball from Le Fée.
Erling Haaland shot off target from inside the six-yard box after Iliman Ndiaye's cross.
Rayan Cherki restored the City lead in the 29th minute from an Antoine Semenyo pass, before Brobbey levelled again, Thomas Meunier supplying him after 33 minutes.
Semenyo made it 3-2 just before half-time, finishing a Marc Guéhi pass from a corner.
Semenyo struck again after 57 minutes, and Brobbey completed his hat-trick two minutes later, set up by Angulo from a set piece.
Rúben Dias headed a Fernández corner off target midway through the second half.
Haaland settled it with nine minutes left, taking a pass from Josko Gvardiol for 5-3.

sections.head: Semenyo among the goals
sections.pitch: Semenyo made three chances across the match and set up the third City goal.
sections.stake: He is test1's man and returned 13 points.

sections.head: Haaland strikes late
sections.pitch: Haaland had four shots in all, one of them the goal that ended the scoring.
sections.stake: He belongs to 123 for six points, and 123 lead test2 38-34 in their head-to-head this period.

sections.head: Gvardiol makes fifth
sections.pitch: Gvardiol laid on the fifth for Haaland.
sections.stake: He was on test31121's bench, so those points did not count.

reports.standfirst: Liverpool won 1-0 at AFC Bournemouth through Alexander Isak, extending their unbeaten start to five and leaving the hosts still chasing a first win.
reports.account:
Evanilson was denied from six yards after 18 minutes, Marcus Tavernier the maker with a cross.
Bradley Barcola forced a save after 33 minutes, Alexander Isak the supplier.
Ryan Christie dragged wide from close range after 53 minutes, Rayan crossing.
Isak settled it after 57 minutes, Liverpool's only goal from three efforts on target.
AFC Bournemouth carved out one clear opening and did not take it.

sections.head: Wirtz withdrawn
sections.pitch: Wirtz made three chances before he was taken off.
sections.stake: He belongs to test1, for whom he scored six points.

sections.head: Christie starts
sections.pitch: Christie made his first league start of the season, had four shots and was then taken off.
sections.stake: He is a free agent.

reports.standfirst: Leeds United and Crystal Palace drew 0-0, Palace keeping their first clean sheet of the season.
reports.account:
Tarik Muharemovic headed a corner off target after eight minutes, Anton Stach crossing.
Jefferson Lerma shot off target from close range from a corner early in the second half.
Tyrick Mitchell had the ball in the net after 52 minutes, only for a video review to rule it out.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin had openings for Leeds and did not take them.
Daichi Kamada headed wide from inside the six-yard box with five minutes left.

sections.head: Trafford keeps it clean
sections.pitch: Trafford made five saves for his clean sheet.
sections.stake: He is test2's keeper for seven points, though 123 lead test2 38-34 in their head-to-head this period.

sections.head: Muharemovic shoots often
sections.pitch: Muharemovic had four shots across the match.
sections.stake: He was on test211's bench.

reports.standfirst: Fulham drew 1-1 with Manchester United, conceding one minute from time to stay in the bottom three and without a win this season.
reports.account:
Gonzalo García shot off target after four minutes, Antonee Robinson the maker.
Bryan Mbeumo headed wide after 11 minutes, Marcus Rashford crossing from a corner.
Bruno Fernandes struck the woodwork after 25 minutes.
Lisandro Martínez turned into his own net after 63 minutes to put Fulham ahead.
Patrick Dorgu came on with six minutes left and had a hand in the leveller.
One minute from time Matheus Cunha drew United level, taking Dorgu's pass and striking it right-footed from outside the box, low into the corner.
Dorgu then headed over from six yards in stoppage time, Mbeumo delivering the cross.
Fulham managed a single goal from six efforts on target and made three clear chances without a return.

sections.head: Cunha finds the corner
sections.pitch: Cunha had three shots and created three chances besides his goal.
sections.stake: He is test2's, and six points spares them a blank.

sections.head: Iwobi creates plenty
sections.pitch: Iwobi made five chances for Fulham before he was taken off.
sections.stake: A free agent.

stories.headline: Spurs left with van Hecke of a comeback
stories.deck: Aston Villa won 3-2 at Tottenham Hotspur

reports.standfirst: Aston Villa won 3-2 at Tottenham for their first win of the season, lifting Emery's side clear of the bottom three, where without a win Spurs remain.
reports.account:
Aston Villa were 3-0 up with 11 minutes left, and Tottenham then scored twice from the 80th minute.
Sávio drew a save with a shot inside the box, set up by Dominic Solanke, in the 11th minute.
Johan Manzambi tested the keeper four minutes later, Victor Lindelöf the provider.
Pedro Porro went off injured in the 19th minute.
Emiliano Buendía saw a shot saved in the 27th minute, Nicolas Jackson supplying him.
Manzambi struck just before the interval, Boubacar Kamara the passer, for 1-0.
Mohammed Kudus came on at half-time.
Kudus had the ball in the net on the hour, made by Solanke, but a video review ruled it out.
Jackson made it 2-0 midway through the second half, Manzambi turning provider on this one.
Buendía added the third with 11 minutes left, John McGinn feeding him from a break down the flank, and he struck it right-footed from outside the box into the top corner.
Conor Gallagher came on with six minutes remaining.
Gallagher pulled one back four minutes from time, Kudus the maker.
Jan Paul van Hecke headed home Andy Robertson's set-piece cross deep into stoppage time for 3-2.

sections.head: Buendía finds range
sections.pitch: Buendía had three efforts across the match and created three chances for others besides his goal.
sections.stake: Notemail has him, worth seven points that day.

sections.head: Manzambi makes mark
sections.pitch: Manzambi took his first league start of the campaign and was withdrawn, having had four attempts and laid on Jackson's second.
sections.stake: He belongs to nobody in the league and has one league goal this season.

sections.head: Sávio busy, unrewarded
sections.pitch: Sávio had three shots and set up four openings for team-mates across the match.
sections.stake: He is going unclaimed in the league.

reports.standfirst: Brighton beat Arsenal 3-0 to push them off top place and hand them a first defeat of the season.
reports.account:
Pascal Groß opened the scoring after 31 minutes. Charalampos Kostoulas laid it back and Groß struck it right-footed from outside the box into the middle of the goal.
Kostoulas doubled it on half-time, finishing a Diego Gómez pass on the break.
Chema Andrés headed in a Groß corner after 57 minutes to make it 3-0.
Pascal Struijk met a De Cuyper corner with a header from close range after 68 minutes, off target.
Riccardo Calafiori then nodded a Declan Rice corner wide from inside the six-yard box, and Kai Havertz headed a Bukayo Saka corner off target too.
Struijk went off injured four minutes from time.
Malick Yalcouyé struck the woodwork after 90 minutes.

sections.head: Groß runs it
sections.pitch: Pascal Groß has three league goals this season and crossed the corner that Chema Andrés headed in.
sections.stake: 123 have him for 11 points, and in their head-to-head this period 123 lead test2 38-34.

sections.head: Kostoulas among the goals
sections.pitch: Charalampos Kostoulas has two league goals this season, had four shots and set up the second before he was taken off.
sections.stake: test31121 have him for eight points.

reports.standfirst: Everton beat 10-man Ipswich 1-0, a fifth match unbeaten for Moyes's side.
reports.account:
Brennan Johnson pulled an early chance off target in the 5th minute, Harrison Armstrong threading him through from inside the box.
Thierno Barry put Everton ahead in the 11th minute, James Tarkowski the provider.
Leif Davis shot over from the six-yard box in the 38th minute, Abdul Fatawu crossing.
Barry had the ball in the net again after 58 minutes, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall the maker, but a video review ruled it out.
Abdul Fatawu was sent off for a second booking midway through the second half.
Dewsbury-Hall put a header wide from the six-yard box with 14 minutes left, Tyler Dibling the crosser.
Emersonn went off injured with nine minutes left.

sections.head: Barry strikes early
sections.pitch: Barry had three efforts across the match and now stands on two league goals this season.
sections.stake: Notemail has him, worth six points.

sections.head: Pickford keeps clean sheet
sections.pitch: Pickford made four saves to keep his goal intact.
sections.stake: test3 has him, at seven points; in the head-to-head this period test4 lead test3 26-24.

reports.standfirst: Newcastle held off Hull 2-1 for a first home win of the season, ending Hull's unbeaten start.
reports.account:
Joe Willock struck after three minutes, converting a Harvey Barnes pass.
Lewis Hall made it 2-0 four minutes later on the break, again teed up by Barnes.
Hall shot off target from the six-yard box after 33 minutes, Jacob Murphy crossing.
Yoane Wissa saw a penalty saved just before the interval.
Sven Botman was denied a header from a Hall cross after 52 minutes.
Mohamed Belloumi shot off target on the break at the other end.
Mohamed-Ali Cho came on midway through the half and pulled one back a minute on. Belloumi threaded him through and he finished left-footed from inside the box, low into the corner.
Sean Steur and then Matias Fernandez-Pardo both went off injured.

sections.head: Barnes turns creator
sections.pitch: Harvey Barnes made both Newcastle goals and three chances in all.
sections.stake: testf has him for eight points.

sections.head: Belloumi busy in defeat
sections.pitch: Mohamed Belloumi had five shots and set up Cho's goal before being taken off.
sections.stake: Notemail has him for four points.

reports.standfirst: Coventry won 1-0 at Nottingham Forest for a first win and first clean sheet of the season, though still in the bottom three.
reports.account:
Dan Ndoye shot off target inside the box after 13 minutes, Neco Williams nodding it to him.
Brandon Thomas-Asante headed a Jay Dasilva cross off target after 28 minutes.
Murillo headed a Williams corner off target from the six-yard box.
Dasilva settled it after 55 minutes. Carl Rushworth found him and he finished left-footed from inside the box into the middle of the goal.
Igor Jesus seemed to have levelled four minutes from time, but a video review ruled it out.

sections.head: Rushworth turns provider
sections.pitch: Carl Rushworth set up Dasilva's winner and kept a clean sheet at the back.
sections.stake: test211 has him on the bench, so his points did not count.

sections.head: Gibbs-White carves without reward
sections.pitch: Morgan Gibbs-White made six chances, none of them converted.
sections.stake: test3 has him.

stories.headline: Chelsea left holding the ball
stories.deck: Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0

reports.standfirst: Brentford beat Chelsea 3-0, three second-half goals lifting Keith Andrews's unbeaten side above the visitors and into third.
reports.account:
Igor Thiago had the first sight of goal after five minutes, meeting a Yehor Yarmoliuk cross with a shot that flew off target.
Pedro Neto replied for Chelsea after 10 minutes, working a chance from a Danny Welbeck pass, but Caoimhín Kelleher saved.
Just before half-time Keane Lewis-Potter was set up by Jaidon Anthony, only for his shot to be turned away.
The opening goal came after 61 minutes. Jannik Schuster headed a corner across goal and Jaidon Anthony finished for 1-0.
With seven minutes left Thiago made it 2-0 on the break, Brentford's second in the space of 11 minutes.
Fábio Carvalho came on three minutes from time.
Four minutes into added time Carvalho added the third. From within the six-yard box he swept a right-footed finish into the top corner for 3-0.

sections.head: Schade threatens
sections.pitch: Kevin Schade had three shots without a goal.
sections.stake: 123 has him for eight points, and 123 lead their head-to-head 38-34 this period.

sections.head: Schuster provides
sections.pitch: Jannik Schuster made the opening goal with his header from the corner.
sections.stake: He is a free agent.

sections.head: Thiago among the goals
sections.pitch: Igor Thiago had three shots across the match, one of them a goal.
sections.stake: He too is a free agent.

stories.headline: Palmer Called A Victim, test1 Left Watching
stories.deck: PFA chief Molango calls Palmer a victim of a sick schedule; the player is test1's asset, no timeline given.
stories.body:
PFA chief executive Maheta Molango has called Cole Palmer a "victim" of a "sick" schedule that asks too much of players. Palmer is test1's, and words of that weight from that office are not the kind test1 ignores over morning coffee.

Nothing in the wire names a match missed or a spell out. So the alarm is the register, not a date: no timeline, no absence flagged, only a warning that the load is heavier than the men carrying it. test1 watches and waits with the rest.

stories.headline: Norwegian Would, If City Went Down
stories.deck: Transfer gossip drags 123's Haaland into relegation talk; City would not sell cheap.
stories.body:
The gossip columns circle Erling Haaland, and it is 123 who reads them closest. City, the wire has it, would not part with him on the cheap were relegation to come to pass. That is a long chain of conditionals, but every link runs through 123's forward line.

Nothing is confirmed and no move is on the table. The cornerstone of the league's heaviest attack stays a City player, under a cloud faint enough that only the owner is squinting at it.

stories.headline: O'Reilly Leaves test3331 In Doubt
stories.deck: test3331's O'Reilly a doubt for England against the Czech Republic on Tuesday
stories.body:
Another of test3331's men joins the international worry list. Nico O'Reilly is a doubt for England's Nations League tie with the Czech Republic on Tuesday, and for test3331 that is one more asset whose Tuesday is now a question rather than a certainty.

No timeline is attached and none is claimed. He is a doubt, not ruled out, and that is where the matter rests until England name a side. For test3331, watching Thomas and McBurnie already framed around the same fixture, the Czech Republic has become the night his squad turns on.

stories.headline: Bellamy Braces For The Norse Menace
stories.deck: Bellamy says Wales belong in Nations League A but expects Norway and Haaland to threaten for years; Haaland is 123's asset.
stories.body:
Craig Bellamy has made his peace with Norway as a coming force, Haaland the point of the spear, and that is 123's concern before it is Wales's. The cornerstone of the league's top-scoring side keeps drawing eyes, this time from a manager reckoning with him rather than for him.

Nothing here changes an ownership or a fixture. Haaland remains 123's, fit enough to loom over an international week, and the only fresh detail is the respect a rival coach is paying him. For this league, that is confirmation, not news.

stories.headline: 123 Left To Sweat On Haaland's Future
stories.deck: City uncertainty puts 123's Haaland in the transfer gossip as Barcelona eye Estevao
stories.body:
The gossip column names 123's most valuable asset, and it names him in the wrong context. Erling Haaland, the forward 123 holds, is drawn into the uncertainty at City in Monday's wire, the sort of paragraph an owner reads twice and then reads again.

Nothing is confirmed and nothing is imminent. The copy monitors interest, no more, and no timeline attaches to any of it. For 123 the material fact is unchanged: Haaland remains his player and remains in the line-up until something firmer than a gossip column says otherwise.

stories.headline: Gakpo Cut Short, test211 In The Dark
stories.deck: Cody Gakpo, owned by test211, hurt on international duty; no timeline given.
stories.body:
Add Cody Gakpo to the international break's casualty list, and add test211 to the managers left waiting on it. His Nations League involvement was curtailed by injury, alongside Bruno Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu, and that is as far as the wire will take us.

What it costs test211, and for how long, nobody has said. No return date has been put on Gakpo. Until one is, test211 plans a Gameweek 6 line-up around a forward whose fitness is another country's business.

stories.headline: Gabriel Takes A New Testament
stories.deck: BBC reports the rise of schoolboy transfers; JJ Gabriel, owned by test31121, is among the assets in play.
stories.body:
The trade in academy footballers is the wire's subject this week, and it lands on one desk in this league. JJ Gabriel, an asset test31121 holds, sits inside the story the BBC has been telling about how the top of the English game now moves its youngest players.

What that means for the footballer, and for test31121's hold on him, the copy does not say. Gabriel is named; a length of absence, a destination, a return date, none of it is on the wire. What is known is that he is in the frame and that test31121 owns him. The rest is for another edition.

stories.headline: Scott Free No Longer For test3331
stories.deck: Chelsea lead the race for Bournemouth's Alex Scott, owned by test3331
stories.body:
Chelsea are said to lead the chase for Alex Scott, and the name matters here because Scott is test3331's. Bournemouth are the sellers in the gossip column; nothing is settled, and a move to Chelsea would not itself change the squad he plays for.

What it flags for test3331 is the shape of an asset whose minutes and role could shift under a bigger club. For now Scott stays where he is, and the interest is noted rather than acted upon.

stories.headline: Trafford Buys Nothing But A Slice Of Nothing
stories.deck: United sell pitch cubes at £125 as debt tops £1bn; test2's Trafford unaffected on the pitch.
stories.body:
United are cutting the ground into squares and asking £125 a piece for them, the same day the club confirmed a debt still north of a billion. None of it lands on test2's team sheet, where the only Trafford that concerns him is the one on the roster and the one worth points.

That name aside, this is a story with no draft consequence: no minutes lost, no return threatened, nothing that touches a scoreline. test2 reads the wire like the rest of us and moves on, his forwards a more pressing matter than a plot of turf.

stories.headline: McBurnie Recalled, test3331 Recouped
stories.deck: Oli McBurnie back in the Scotland fold, a lift for test3331's forward stock; Clarke, the man who left him out, belongs to test211.
stories.body:
test3331 owns McBurnie, and the forward is back in Scotland's reckoning after being overlooked and written off. He returns with something to prove, which for this league means minutes and the goals that follow them.

The man who left him out, Steve Clarke, sits on test211's books. Two managers on either side of the same selection call. Nothing here is settled, and nothing on the pitch has happened yet.

stories.headline: Predicted Line-Ups: Gameweek 6
stories.deck: Every club's expected starting eleven for the round, match by match.
stories.body: All 10 of the round's matches, with both sides named.

stories.headline: Cherki Sees test4 Home By Two
stories.deck: test4 edged test3 26-24, Cherki's seven the top score in a tie where Pickford matched him.
stories.body:
Cherki settled it. His seven led test4, and with Justin adding six behind him the margin held at two. E.Le Fée weighed in with five; the tail of Gray, Mbeumo and N.Williams gave only two apiece, but the top of the line-up did enough.

test3 will feel this one. Pickford matched Cherki with seven from goal, and Ndiaye's five kept the chase alive, but the forwards let him down. Emersonn, Gonzalo and Gibbs-White managed two each, and Grimes three, and none of it closed the gap.

Two points, three men on two. test3 had the goalkeeper and the midfield return he wanted and still came up short where he needed his strikers most.

stories.headline: Groß Domestic Product Sinks test2
stories.deck: 123 beat test2 38-34, Groß's eleven the top score in a four-point tie
stories.body:
Groß settled it. Eleven from the midfielder led every man on the pitch, and Schade's eight behind him gave 123 the top two returns of the tie. Haaland added six. That trio alone matched most of what test2 could muster across a whole side.

test2 had Hall for eight and Trafford for a clean-sheet seven at the back, and needed his forwards to follow. They did not. Cunha's six and Isak's five were fair, but Havertz managed two and Lukić the same, and a front line built to haul delivered a middle-order.

Four points in it, and test2 will look at the bottom of his own sheet before anything 123 did. Two twos from Havertz and Lukić is the difference in a tie this tight. Groß was always going to be hard to beat; being beaten by your own attack blanking is the harder one to take.

stories.headline: Wirtz Kept In, test1 Kept Happy
stories.deck: Liverpool won't sanction a Wirtz exit, so test1 keeps his asset.
stories.body:
The gossip pages have Barcelona ruling out Alvarez and Chelsea circling an English midfield pair, but the line that matters here is Liverpool's refusal to let Wirtz go. He belongs to test1, and for now he stays exactly where test1 wants him.

Nothing in the copy touches his fitness or his minutes, so nothing here does either. A door that might have opened has been shut, and test1's squad sheet reads the same tonight as it did this morning.

stories.headline: test1 Bears The Saka Scar
stories.deck: Saka, owned by test1, speaks of England's lingering World Cup wound; no injury reported.
stories.body:
Bukayo Saka carries the paper's interest wherever he goes, and he belongs to test1. This week the winger spoke of a "scar" left by England's World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina, a wound the squad still carry.

Nothing here touches the team sheet. Saka is fit, Saka is talking, and test1 has an asset unbruised by anything but memory. The words are national; the ownership is local.

stories.headline: Thomas Called Up, test3331 Left Waiting
stories.deck: Martha Thomas, owned by test3331, recalled to Scotland squad for World Cup play-offs against the Czech Republic.
stories.body:
Martha Thomas is back in a Scotland squad for the first time in nearly a year, named for next month's World Cup round one play-offs against the Czech Republic. For test3331, that is a squad player pulled into international duty at the worst end of the calendar.

The tie is the round-one play-off, so test3331 knows the fixture but not the toll. Whether Thomas features, and for how long, is not for us to say here. What is settled is that test3331's asset now answers to a Scotland shirt.

stories.headline: Semenyo Says So
stories.deck: Semenyo's two goals and an assist top the gameweek 5 team of the week, picked 1-2-5-3.
stories.body:
Semenyo is the man of the week and there is no argument to be had. Two goals and an assist across a full ninety, a forward doing the forward's job and then some, and nobody else in the side matched the sheer weight of it. test1 have the top score and they have earned the top billing.

The back is thin by design and richer for it. Hall took a goal from defence for test2, and Tarkowski paired an assist with a clean sheet for testf, the sort of line a manager builds a season on. Between them and behind them sits the week's real story: Rushworth kept his clean sheet, found an assist and made two saves, and test211 left him on the bench. A goalkeeper does everything asked and his own manager looks the other way. He is not alone in that indignity, because Gomez did the same in midfield for test31, an assist and a clean sheet watched from the sidelines by the man who owns him.

The middle is where the depth lives. Groß gave 123 a goal, an assist and a clean sheet, the complete midfielder's return, and Barnes matched him for creation with two assists for testf. Willock took his goal, Wirtz found his assist and his clean sheet inside seventy minutes, and the five hang together as a unit rather than a collection.

The front carries the rest. Kostoulas gave test31121 a goal, an assist and a clean sheet in seventy-five minutes, and Schade turned two assists into a forward's afternoon for 123 without troubling the scorers himself. It is a line that created as much as it finished.

Unlucky to miss out, and it is close, is anyone who wanted a fifth forward, but the shape does not allow it. Nobody outscored Semenyo, so nobody displaces him, and the two benched men keep their places on merit whatever their managers thought.

And finally, a word about the two managers who sat their own best men. Rushworth and Gomez did everything a manager could ask and were trusted with none of it. The team of the week found room for both. Their owners did not.

stories.headline: 123 Count On A Slender Margin
stories.deck: 123 top the rankings on 77 scored despite a split week, beating test2 by four; four sides on 3 points, six yet to register.
stories.body:
Five weeks in and the table lies to you. Four managers sit level on three points, a single win and a single defeat apiece, and the arithmetic cannot separate them. The football can. 123 put 77 on the board and squeezed test2 out by four; that is a ceiling nobody else has touched, and a 1-0-1 record does it no justice. test2, for their part, lost the game and still outscored two managers above them in points if not in the standings.

Below the line sit six managers with nothing beside their name. Zeroes across the board, no games logged, no evidence either way. That is not a verdict, it is an absence of one, and until they play they are ranked on faith and little else. test3 top-scored among the beaten and are better than a two-point loss to test4 suggests; test4 won the game and know it was the closer thing than the scoreline reads.

No game, no evidence, no complaint from me until there is something to weigh.

Bottom by the table and bottom by me until a match tells me otherwise.
